why: The project's 300 MW load assumes an N+1 backup design of 121 diesel generators at 2,500 kW each, yielding an estimated NOx potential to emit of 1,067 tpy, which exceeds the 100 tpy major-source threshold under 40 CFR 70.2 and triggers a federal Title V operating permit requirement. Washington County adopted Ordinance ORD-2026-12 effective June 30, 2026, imposing a countywide moratorium on data center applications for six months (computed expiration December 29, 2026), but the site lies within Hagerstown city which has its own zoning, leaving the moratorium's jurisdictional reach unconfirmed. The moratorium's duration is contested: the draft ordinance specifies six months, while the Moratorium Nation dataset states a twelve-month moratorium, creating a source conflict about the actual adopted duration. The Title V major-source determination relies on assumed generator specifications (Tier 2 diesel, 500 hours/year) that have not been verified for this project, and the actual backup power design could alter the NOx potential to emit. Because the county moratorium's applicability within city limits and its duration are unresolved, and the federal air permit requirement depends on unverified design assumptions, the project's viability cannot be determined without confirming these key facts.
